title: Knowledge check: Integrating External APIs

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed for “Integrating External APIs”?
options: A complete substitute for server-side validation
A guarantee that every database write succeeds atomically
A feature that is always enabled without configuration
questions.explanation: The supplied Django curriculum lists “HTTP requests to external services” under lesson 157, “Integrating External APIs”. The lesson connects this item to the practical Django workflow for email, background work, and external services.

questions.prompt: Which workflow best supports reliable work on “Integrating External APIs”?
options: Assume the browser is trusted and skip server-side checks.
Copy a production secret into the source file so every environment matches.
Publish an example before checking framework/version compatibility.
Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
questions.answer_key: Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
questions.explanation: Small reproducible examples, server-side validation where relevant, and explicit positive/negative checks help distinguish expected behavior from assumptions. Version, environment, and boundary cases should be documented.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most appropriate when applying “Integrating External APIs” in a real application?
options: Treat a successful HTTP status as proof a remote payment is settled.
Expose all internal error messages and credentials to clients.
Validate external input, set timeouts, handle failures, and make retried work idempotent.
Retry every error forever with no backoff or uniqueness check.
questions.answer_key: Validate external input, set timeouts, handle failures, and make retried work idempotent.
questions.explanation: The lesson is part of Email, Background Work, and External Services. Select the approach that supports correctness, safe handling of failures, and verifiable behavior; see the linked official documentation for version-specific details.

notes: Answer keys and explanations remain in the server-side course repository. The existing CodeLeaf GET handler strips answers until grading; this course does not expose solutions in public lesson content.
